one_month_reasoning: No NVDA print in the window: Q3 FY27 is expected ~Nov 17 (some calendars say Nov 25), both after Nov 4 (28). Inside the window: TSMC Q3 (mid-Oct), hyperscaler Q3 reports and 2027 capex guides (Oct 27-30) against ~$1.3T projected 2027 capex with negative FCF at most of them (17), the FOMC on Oct 28 (~17% hike priced per the supervisor's check) and the Nov 3 midterms. All are two-sided. Short-horizon regularities pull both ways: the stock ran ~12% in under three weeks (Form 4 tax-withholding price $212.17 on Sep 16 (30) to $236.88) and sits at its 52-week high, which argues for some reversal risk, against positive momentum. No edge strong enough to tilt, so a near-symmetric lognormal at 38%/3.5 = 10.9% monthly vol with a hair of reversal: P(>= $236.88) = 0.48.

fair_value.method: Blend of horizon P/E (consistent Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29 NTM EPS $16.7 x 16x + $2.35 balance-sheet/contingent adjustment = $270, 50%), FCF yield ($16.7 x 70% conversion = $11.7/share at 5.0% + $2.35 = $236, 30%) and mid-cycle EPS ($13.6 x 16x + $2.35 = $220, 20%) = ~$250.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Horizon NTM EPS (Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29) $16.7 x 16x = $267.7, + $2.35/share net cash, haircut equity stakes, less expected guarantee and commitment losses

inputs_detail.derivation: FY28 guide ~+70% revenue (supply-constrained), GM 72-73% (6, confirmed in the call per supervisor); I haircut to ~+65% and ~52-53% net margin on ~23.9B shares -> ~$14.4-15.1. Consensus $15.5-15.7 (7), so $15.0 is a ~4.5% skeptic haircut. Unchanged from round 1.

Sharp deceleration after +65-70%: hyperscaler FCF negative in 2027 (17), ASIC volumes projected to pass GPUs in 2027 (23), lenders underwriting GPUs over 3-4 years (13), depreciation critique (11). FY29 of $16.8 is below the Q4 FY28 run-rate, i.e. a skeptic flattening in CY2028.

inputs_detail.input: Horizon NTM EPS (Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29, consistent with today's 19.3-19.7x basis)
inputs_detail.derivation: $8.50 H2 FY28 + $8.2 H1 FY29. Round 1 used 0.25 FY28 + 0.75 FY29 ($16.35), shifted one quarter vs today's NTM window (supervisor). On the consistent window my EPS rises slightly because FY28 is back-half loaded.

Today 19.34x NTM (8). At-scale anchor AVGO 20.49x / TSM 20.65x (9), median ~20.6x. 16x = ~22% discount to that pair, at the top of the 12-22% range the supervisor called partly justified, for vendor-financing features AVGO does not carry at the same scale: $105B lease guarantee, $25B equity investment commitments, $94B of stakes largely in AI customers, payment terms up to one year and DSO 45->60 (2,29). Round 1's 17x leaned on a 'historical floor 17-20x' claim (4) that the supervisor discounted, so I drop it. Break-even for a flat year is 236.88/16.7 = 14.2x.

Net cash: cash $22.4B + marketable debt $34.1B - debt $33.4B = $23.1B = +$0.97. Equity stakes (marketable $42.8B + non-marketable $51.2B = $94.0B, excluded from non-GAAP EPS) at a 50% skeptic haircut = +$1.97. SB Energy/OpenAI guarantee: cap $105B ($4.39/share), effective from FY29 as leases commence, covering the resale/reletting shortfall on OpenAI default (32,33); expected loss 20% default x 30% shortfall = 6% x $105B = $6.3B, plus 10% of $3.5B other guarantees = -$0.28. $25B equity commitments at 30% overpayment haircut = -$0.31. Net +$2.35 on 23.9B shares. A severe case (50% default x 50% shortfall on $105B) is -$1.10/share: the guarantee matters as a demand-quality signal, not as a direct hit to value.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: $399B NTM NI x 70% conversion = $279B / 23.9B shares = $11.68/share at 5.0% yield = $233.6, + $2.35

DSO rose 45->60 on extended terms up to one year, AR $63.1B with five customers at 70%, supply commitments $279B (2). I take H1's ~70%, down from round 1's 85%, which the filings do not support.

NVDA's AA bonds yield 4.25% (2028) to 5.625% (2056) (20). 5.0% is tighter than the ~4.4% FCF yield implied by 16x P/E at 70% conversion; the gap is deliberate and prices the risk that conversion stays depressed by vendor financing.
Q1 $1.87 + Q2 $2.22 reported; Q3 ~$2.45 (consensus $2.47 (4)); Q4 ~$2.55 with GM at its 71-72% trough (6), below consensus $2.73.

bear.story: During 2027 hyperscalers, FCF-negative (17), signal 2028 capex flattening; ASIC share gains (23) and lender skepticism on GPU residual values (13) cap pricing; GM stuck near 71% (6); conversion stays ~40% as extended terms and customer financing grow (29). Horizon NTM EPS falls to ~$13 and the market applies ~12x (between MU and TSM) -> ~$155. The guarantee and the $94B of customer-linked stakes become a narrative overhang even though the direct expected cost is ~$1/share at worst.

base.story: FY28 delivers ~+65% revenue and ~$15 EPS; FY29 seen at low-teens growth; consistent NTM EPS ~$16.7 at ~15.3x (another ~4 turns of compression) plus ~$2 of balance sheet -> ~$258, a high-single-digit gain where de-rating eats most of the earnings growth.

bull.story: Supply-constrained demand lets FY28 beat +70% with GM back at 73%; NTM EPS ~$19.5 at ~18.3x as Rubin extends the lead and conversion normalises -> ~$360.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 6.1x (MU) to 128.9x (ARM), interquartile ~20.6x-47.2x. EV/EBITDA figures (median 44.8x, range 10.5x-305.6x) are TRAILING, not forward; they are not comparable with forward EV/EBITDA medians (~28.5x) and are not used in my valuation. NVDA today 19.34x forward P/E (NTM Q3 FY27-Q2 FY28), 27.95x trailing EV/EBITDA. At-scale anchor AVGO/TSM median 20.57x.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 16x consistent-basis NTM at horizon: inside the peer range, below the 12-name median and ~22% below the AVGO/TSM at-scale anchor (20.57x); break-even for a flat year is ~14.2x on my EPS.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The 12-name median is inflated by early-ramp earners (ARM, AMD, MRVL, ANET); I anchor on AVGO/TSM, the only peers at NVDA's scale and earnings stage. The ~22% horizon discount rests on factors visible in filings that persist past the horizon because they are contractual: (a) the $105B SB Energy/OpenAI guarantee runs 20 years from FY29 (2,33); (b) $25B of equity investment commitments and $94B of stakes largely in AI customers (2); (c) extended payment terms up to one year, DSO 45->60, five customers = 70% of AR, FCF conversion ~70% in H1 and ~39% in Q2 (2,29); (d) GM reset from ~75% to 72-73% on memory costs (6). AVGO sells to the same hyperscalers, so concentration alone is not a discount reason (supervisor); the vendor-financing items (a)-(c) are what NVDA carries and AVGO does not at similar scale. Not a claim of inferior franchise quality, and no sell-side outperformance call is used.

thesis_break_reason: $160 is below the 52-week low ($164.27), ~13x today's NTM EPS ($12.00-12.25) and ~9.6x my consistent-basis Oct-2027 NTM EPS ($16.7). Compression alone cannot get there while EPS holds (a flat year already needs ~14.2x), so trading there would mean the FY28/FY29 EPS path is breaking: a hyperscaler capex cut, ASIC displacement, GM well below the 71-72% trough, or a customer credit event that shows in receivables or the OpenAI-linked guarantee.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's checks changed three things. (1) NTM basis: today's 19.3-19.7x is on Q3 FY27-Q2 FY28; I restate horizon EPS on Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29 = $8.50 + $8.2 = $16.7 (round 1: $16.35 shifted). (2) FCF conversion: the CFO commentary shows Q2 FCF $21.3B vs $54-60B NI and H1 FCF $69.9B (~70%), so 85% becomes 70%. (3) The 'historical floor 17-20x' I leaned on was discounted, so I re-anchor the multiple on AVGO/TSM (20.57x) with a ~22% discount for contractual vendor-financing items and take 16x rather than 17x. I fixed my EV/EBITDA comps label (trailing, not forward; not used in valuation). As asked, I quantified the contingent book per share from the 10-Q: net cash +$0.97, stakes at 50% +$1.97, guarantee expected loss -$0.28 (cap $4.39), commitments -$0.31, net +$2.35; the guarantee covers the reletting shortfall on OpenAI default and only starts in FY29, so its value hit is small and its real weight is as a signal of financed demand. New skeptic-lane checks found nothing alarming: September Form 4s show Huang's tax withholding and a gift, not open-market sales, and CFO 10b5-1 sales of ~36k shares; litigation is unaccrued. Fair value falls from $261 to ~$250. Why a skeptic still sees a flat-to-up base: a flat year needs ~14.2x on my EPS, a ~27% de-rating from 19.5x that only an EPS break would bring, so the downside case is the bear (EPS ~$13 at ~12x, 25%), not plain compression. Scenarios $155/25%, $258/50%, $360/25% give mean ~$258, median ~$254; the ladder is a lognormal mixture (sigmas 17-24%) with a slightly fatter left tail than lognormal: P(>=$237) 0.59, P(<$166) 0.16. Net ladder change is small because the lower fair value is offset by the higher consistent-basis EPS. I disagree with the supervisor's 16.5x only modestly: I keep a lower 16x because the vendor-financing items are contractual and outlast the horizon.
